title: ReactionEvent
description: One observed reader reaction. The reaction channel is the ONLY input from which reader-dependent salience can be computed: identity/provenance is reader-independent and computable from text, salience is reader-dependent and computable from no text at all (HANDOFF section 1.6, three independent failed attempts). A ReactionEvent is an OBSERVATION OF A READER, never an engine inference, so it lives in its own append-only log rather than the semantic ledger — it carries no operator, no prior_id, and no operator_epoch, and it may never mint an observation, referent, hypothesis, or task. ts and seq are HOST-SUPPLIED and never generated engine-side, because the engine must contain no clock (same discipline as SemanticEvent@1) or replay stops being byte-identical.

reaction_id.description: Content address of every other field. reaction:sha256:<64 hex>.

ts.description: Host-supplied milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The engine never reads an ambient clock.

seq.description: Host-supplied per-session monotone counter. Required, and not redundant with ts: batched reactions routinely share a millisecond, and without seq two otherwise-identical reactions would collapse to one content address and be refused as duplicates. seq also gives the log a total order that does not depend on clock resolution.

kind.description: The nine observed reaction kinds. Note that skip and abandon are disengagement, not engagement — nothing in this spec assigns them a sign, because weighting kinds against each other is an inference and inference is deliberately out of scope until the channel has collected data.

block_id.description: The content-addressed block the reaction landed on.

extent.description: Sub-block span the reaction covered, or null when the reaction is whole-block.

context.description: What was on screen when the reaction happened. Required so a reaction can later be read against its alternatives: a dwell on the only visible block means something different from a dwell on one of twelve.

scale.description: The altitude/scale the reader was at. A string, not a number, because unit size is not yet a swept parameter (HANDOFF Part 5).

payload.description: Kind-specific detail (query text, dwell ms, scrub delta). Deliberately unconstrained: the channel collects first and the shapes are not yet known.
